result.title: When Does an Added Planning Capability Create Operational Value? An Observable Evidence Standard
result.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables. Accepted and presented at the 3rd IEOM World Congress on Industrial Engineering and Operations Management, Irvine, California, USA, October 13-15, 2026. Code and reproduction materials: https://github.com/yvonnexu442/planning-capability-evidence-standard/releases/tag/v1.0-camera-ready
result.summary: Industrial artificial intelligence (AI) planning systems combine predictive models, optimization logic, controls, and governance rules, but improvement in the complete policy does not show whether one addition made an independent contribution or whether that contribution justifies its burden. We address this attribution problem with an observable evidence standard that separates opportunity to act, executed-plan change, operational consequence, equivalence, uncertainty, and operating scope. Using forecast-to-plan replay on Favorita, M5, and Walmart data, we apply the standard to heterogeneous planning additions. Three limits of single-indicator evaluation emerge. First, a composite policy can conceal negligible component contribution: one control changed only 15 of 681 executed plans. Second, changing execution does not guarantee stable benefit: the evaluated multi-period capability helped in several long-lead settings but was 7.6% more costly under tight capacity. Third, indirect evidence can prioritize review but cannot complete attribution. Independent runs produced different paths in 19 of 599 cases that a rule-based check predicted would be unchanged. Although a lower-cost diagnostic matched the full-evaluation winner in only 55.0% of cases, it selected an option within the $10^{-6}$ cost-equivalence tolerance in 79.5%; the remaining cases prevented the proxy from authorizing acceptance. These experiments establish capability-level contribution evidence; the organization completes the value decision by weighing it against implementation and sustaining burden. The resulting capability evidence record links the observations to validation, deployment scope, fallback, monitoring, redesign, and retirement decisions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对工业 AI 规划系统中「新增规划能力是否带来独立价值」的归因问题，提出一套可观测证据标准，把行动机会、执行计划改变、运行后果、等价性、不确定性与适用范围分开，并用 Favorita、M5、Walmart 的预测—计划回放检验多种异构规划能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「整体策略改善不等于单组件有独立贡献」「代理诊断只能提示审查、不能完成归因」等结论，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK 等步骤的贡献分配与证据门槛提供评价框架参考，可供核查能否迁移到 latent 推理的消融与等价判定。
